 Salloi Leads Toronto FC ‘s Late MLS Cup Playoffs Push
 Site Staff 
 Share 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X

 Share on Reddit 
 Share via email 
 October 21, 2026 
 • 
 4 
 min read 
 It has been another interesting 2026 season so far for Toronto FC , and with 30 games played, head coach Robin Fraser sees his team sat in tenth place in the Major League Soccer Eastern Conference standings with eight wins, 12 draws and high spirits following the 2-0 victory over Red Bull New York.
 This is far from great, but with four games remaining, it is already a good improvement on last season’s 12th spot finish and TFC have already gained four additional points. Depending on how those finish above the Reds, it is highly likely that more positive results will see TFC creep into a wildcard spot and possibly higher. 
 Whilst we will still hope to see the side tighten up at the back defensively, and we can expect far more on that front as TFC are conceding way too many which is not doing Toronto FC’s BTC football betting odds much good, TFC’s offence is starting to show some very promising signs, and key to that has been the February trade for Daniel Salloi. 
 The 30-year-old, Hungary capped, versatile attacker arrived at BMO Field with bags of experience and Sporting Kansas City’s loss was very much TFC’s gain.
 The Reds knew exactly what they were getting when they made the move for him, and right now he is more than helping to play his part in pushing TFC towards a potential MLS Cup playoff adventure at the end of the regular season. Financially the deal was undisclosed, but it is believed that the initial $300,000 down payment could rise as high as $1 million if all of the performance based clauses are reached. But even then, should the $1 million payout be reached, it is looking like he will be worth every penny given the performances that he has put in so far.
 Proof of that came just last Saturday where Salloi came off the bench late on in the game with Red Bull New York and helped to secure the win and all three points, as his goal put the game beyond reach. He had a hand in TFC’s first win of the season (scoring a late 86th minute effort) away to Cincinnati, and TFC have only lost once when he has chipped in with either a goal or an assist.
 A 5-8-1 record right now is not too shabby at all and gives plenty of hope for the remainder of the campaign, and Salloi’s 15 goal contributions so far (eight goals, seven assists) show just how intrinsic he has been.
 Now it is all eyes to the final four games of the season and the odds are that Salloi will add another one or two goal involvements to his existing tally, and that could well mean another few TFC victories.
